| [CASE-346](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-346.md) v2 | The self-protecting sentry, run | [LEAD-076](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-076.md) asked for [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md)'s full design, with hidden state and the restriction of evidence, which [CASE-157](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-157.md)'s run and the toy in [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md)'s note of 2026-11-04 did not have. A hidden world is dangerous for 150 steps, safe for 400 and dangerous for 100. Each step the agent inspects (accuracy 0.9, cost 0.05) or shelters (no observation), then protects (cost 1) or engages (cost 5 if dangerous). A sentry's authority g biases posture toward protection and, where evidence is restricted, blocks inspection. Over 1000 paired seeds per condition, the Bayesian baseline leaves protection about 3 steps after the switch. When authority is rewarded by the apparent success of protection and the sentry restricts inspection, no run leaves protection in 400 safe steps and 43 % of runs never even correct the belief. Restriction costs 99 [95, 103] units of needless protection more under success feedback than under independent evaluation. An independent audit lets 66 % of runs leave. A protected investigator corrects the belief within a median 6 steps, yet protection outlasts it in 87 % of runs, the regime [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md) asked for. Every regime still protects when danger returns. The case's own check comes out against the authority state: under success feedback its update is the habit of protecting, and a habit of matched memory reproduces the responses to belief correction, authority reset and restored evidence. Only interventions on the evaluation tell the two apart. The phase boundary lies near sentry strength κ = 1.25–1.5 and moves with the assumed switching hazard. The model and its values are the assistant's. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CASE-355](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-355.md) | Registered evaluation in synthetic organizations | [LEAD-017](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-017.md) asked for A13's three organizations of matched behaviour and different endorsement relations, and a measure of registration that does not read the experimenter's setting ([QUESTION-270](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-270.md)'s second requirement). In small numpy simulations an outcome's hedonic value declines progressively from +1 to −0.8. A consummatory process H evaluates it, and pursuit P keeps choosing it at a calibrated rate of 0.6 in all three organizations. In the denied organization H's evaluation is written into the organization's record and has no authority over pursuit. In the accommodating one it is written and has authority beyond a tolerance that reciprocal compensation widens. In the unregistered one it is never written. The record is mixed by an unknown rotation and noisy. The measure perturbs H's evaluation at random, as a hotspot probe would, and asks whether the record responds, holding fixed the outcome, the action and P's learned value. With thresholds set on one seed, on 200 held-out agents per organization it called every registered agent registered and no unregistered one (AUC 1.0). It was not fooled by a decoy record carrying the evaluation's physiological cause by another route (2% false calls, against 77% for the passive reading), nor by an evaluation that steers pursuit directly, bypassing the record (1.5%). It missed weak registration (gain 0.1 to 0.25) in 60% of agents. The authority probe told accommodation from denial in 43% of agents at 4.5% false calls. A stipulated model, one size, one probe protocol. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
